item.title: A disproof of the El-Zahar--Erdos conjecture
item.description: El-Zahar and Erd\H{o}s asked whether every graph of bounded clique number and sufficiently large chromatic number contains two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs, each of large chromatic number, with no edge between them. We give a negative answer even for triangle-free graphs. For every integer $g \ge 4$, we show by a probabilistic argument that there exist graphs of girth at least $g$ and arbitrarily large chromatic number in which any two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs that each require at least seven colors… — Chenghua Liu, Boning Meng — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.DM / cs.CC / cs.DS

item.title: A disproof of the van Emde Boas--Kruyswijk conjecture on the Davenport constant
item.description: The Davenport constant $D(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ is the smallest positive integer $\ell$ such that every sequence $S$ with terms from $G$ and with length $|S| \ge \ell$ has a nontrivial zero-sum subsequence. A long-standing conjecture, first proposed by van Emde Boas and Kruyswijk in 1969, states that $D(C_n^r)=r(n-1)+1$ for all positive integers $n$ and $r$. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture by showing that $D(C_6^r)>5r+1$ for every $r\ge23$. — Weidong Gao, Alfred Geroldinger, Guoqing Wang, Xiangneng Zeng — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.DM / cs.CC / cs.DS / arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / RA / AC

item.title: Sharp boundary regularity for planar minimal graphs with analytic Dirichlet data
item.description: We study the boundary behavior of generalized (BV) solutions of the Dirichlet problem for the minimal surface equation over a bounded set \(\Omega\). Such a generalized solution is always the graph of a smooth function \(v\) inside \(\Omega\), but might carry a vertical part over \(\partial\Omega\), which records the gap between the prescribed Dirichlet datum \(g\) and the boundary trace \(h\) attained by \(v\). When \(\Omega\) is a bounded real-analytic planar domain and \(g\) is real analytic we prove that… — Camillo De Lellis, Guido De Philippis, Alessio Figalli — arXiv math.AP / CA / FA / CV / SP / OA / arXiv math.DG / MG / GN / GR / QA / arXiv: ricci

item.title: A counterexample to the Harper-norm silver-mean conjecture
item.description: The silver-mean conjecture formulated in Gerhold and Shalit 2022 states that the norm $E(\alpha)$ of the Harper operator attains its minimum at the silver mean $\alpha = \sqrt{2}-1$. We show that this conjecture is wrong by constructing an explicit rational point with a smaller Harper-norm value: $E(181/437)<2.591046794 — Evgeny Shchukin, Peter van Loock — arXiv math.AP / CA / FA / CV / SP / OA

item.title: A counterexample to Molchan's orthant persistence conjecture
item.description: We refute Molchan's conjecture that the persistence probability of the isotropic fractional Brownian field on $[0,R]^d$ satisfies $p_{d,H}(R)=R^{-d(1-H)+o(1)}$ as $R\to\infty$. We prove $$ \limsup_{d\to\infty}\limsup_{R\to\infty} \frac{-\log p_{d,H}(R)}{d\log R} \le 1-\frac{49}{48}H+o(H), \qquad H\downarrow 0. $$ Thus the conjecture fails for every sufficiently small fixed Hurst parameter in all sufficiently large dimensions. A finite-step Gaussian interpolation inequality on the exact positive sphere is proved… — Svyatoslav Novikov — arXiv math.PR / DS / ST / OC / NA

item.title: Cosmic Censorship in the Landscape of SUSY-Broken AdS Vacua
item.description: We investigate signatures of weak cosmic censorship in non-supersymmetric vacua of both IIA and IIB string theory. In particular, we examine the Penrose Inequality, which can be proven holographically using Ryu-Takayanagi, and can be independently proven in SUSY AdS vacua for spherically symmetric initial data. We prove that any EFT of scalars coupled to gravity in AdS, including in particular those of string compactifications, satisfies both the Penrose Inequality and a positive mass theorem if a function that… — Netta Engelhardt, Richard Nally — arXiv: swampland

item.title: On Hilbert's tenth problem for number fields
item.description: Given a quadratic number field $K$ we show that the $abc$ conjecture over $K$ implies that $\mathbb{Z}$ is Diophantine in $K$ and, hence, a negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over $K$. More generally, the same conclusions hold for an arbitrary number field $K$ provided that the $abc$ conjecture holds over $K$ and that there is an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ whose rank is positive and does not increase over $K$. — Hector Pasten, Xavier Vidaux — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.DM / cs.CC / cs.DS / arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / RA / AC / arXiv: elliptic

item.title: Singular layer neural networks for the Navier-Stokes equations at small viscosity
item.description: We develop neural network methods for the two-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations at a small viscosity $\varepsilon > 0$, whose accuracy is uniform in $\varepsilon$ and whose residual is evaluated on a grid that does not resolve the vorticity boundary layer. In the vorticity-stream function formulation with the slip boundary conditions, a vorticity layer of width $\sqrt{\varepsilon}$ forms along the walls. The trial function of the singular layer Physics-Informed Neural Network (sl-PINN) contains… — Teng-Yuan Chang, Gung-Min Gie, Youngjoon Hong, Chang-Yeol Jung — arXiv: navier

item.title: A proof of the Reinhardt conjecture
item.description: We prove the Reinhardt conjecture: among centrally symmetric convex disks in the plane, the smoothed regular octagon has the least optimal lattice packing density, and equality holds precisely for its nonsingular affine images. The proof combines explicit bounds on the number of control arcs, local cost inequalities and rigorous finite verification of the remaining switching types. — Fei Xue — arXiv: sphere packing

item.title: Proof of the polygonal Saint-Venant inequality conjectured by Polya--Szego
item.description: We prove the polygonal Saint--Venant inequality conjectured by P\'olya and Szeg\"o: for every $n\geq 3$, among (possibly non--convex) polygons of prescribed area with at most $n$ sides, the regular $n$-gon uniquely maximizes torsional rigidity. The proof is purely analytic and stems from the local version of the result given in our previous paper: it combines an area--angle proportional partition of a polygon, inspired by Solynin and Zalgaller, with a sharp comparison for the mixed torsional rigidity of the… — Beniamin Bogosel, Dorin Bucur, Ilaria Fragala — arXiv math.AP / CA / FA / CV / SP / OA

item.title: Maximality of the Došen-Petrić Boolean Category
item.description: We prove that the zero-identity Boolean category of Došen and Petrić, freely generated by a nonempty set of propositional variables, is maximal. Every congruence preserved by the operations on morphisms and by uniform formula substitution either is equality or identifies every pair of parallel morphisms. This disproves their conjecture that the category is not maximal. We give two proofs that use Boolean Coherence and uniform formula substitution to derive equality of the product projections from an… — Florian Lengyel — arXiv: lean

item.title: ER=EPR and IMP wormholes in quantum gravity
item.description: We analyze and refine the ER=EPR conjecture by studying IMP (Isenberg, Mazzeo and Pollack \cite{Isenberg:2001qe}) wormholes in QFT and quantum gravity, in the AdS/CFT context. IMP wormholes are solutions to the Einstein equations constructed from another general solution of Einstein's equations by gluing a handle on a Cauchy slice with a constant mean curvature, so that the initial data on the slice does not change in the regions away from the handle. This is made possible by using what is called the conformal… — Eyoab Bahiru — arXiv hep-th / arXiv: ads cft

item.title: On metric multiplicative Diophantine approximation
item.description: Gallagher's theorem (1962) gives a Khintchine-type dichotomy for the Lebesgue measure of the set of multiplicatively $\psi$-approximable points in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n \geq 2$, for monotonic functions $\psi$. We establish this dichotomy for arbitrary functions $\psi$, proving a conjecture of Beresnevich, Haynes, and Velani (2013). — Manuel Hauke-Treuer, Felipe A. Ramirez — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / RA / AC

item.title: Quanta Books Releases Six Math Essentials by Terence Tao
item.description: In the book, the Fields Medalist introduces six core ideas that shaped the field of mathematics. — Thomas Sumner — Simons Foundation

item.title: Combinatorial Bloch-Gieseker inequalities on toric surfaces
item.description: We give a combinatorial proof of the Bloch-Gieseker inequalities in the special case of ample toric vector bundles on toric surfaces via a new rearrangement inequality for planar curves. Using this we establish the Hodge package for combinatorial analogues of cohomology rings of ample projective bundles over toric surfaces which don't appear to arise from matroidal constructions. — Hunter Spink — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / RA / AC

item.title: Complete monotonicity of Laplace transform ratios: Density criteria for self-decomposability and additive decomposition
item.description: We prove a complete monotonicity (CM) theorem for ratios of Laplace transforms: if the denominator function is logarithmically convex and the quotient of the two functions is monotone, then the corresponding quotient of Laplace transforms (or, in the opposite monotonicity case, its derivative) is CM. As probabilistic consequences, we obtain density-level criteria for self-decomposability (SD) and additive decomposition (AD) of positive distributions, together with a short proof of the classical Steutel theorem… — Zhong-Xuan Mao, Jing-Feng Tian — arXiv math.PR / DS / ST / OC / NA

item.title: Twist-4 QCD Factorization for One-Point Correlators at Next-to-Leading Order in Electron-Ion Collisions
item.description: Energy and charge correlators have emerged as powerful, infrared- and collinear-safe (IRC-safe) observables for probing QCD dynamics in the vacuum, established within the leading-twist factorization formalism. However, their IRC safety and factorization properties in a nuclear medium, where higher-twist contributions are critically enhanced, remain unproven. In this letter, we present the first proof of next-to-leading order QCD factorization for one-point energy and charge correlators (OPEC and OPCC) in… — Omar Elgedawy, Zhong-Bo Kang, Hongxi Xing — arXiv hep-ph / hep-ex / hep-lat

item.title: Orbit-averaged spinning and eccentric binary black holes: Hamiltonian and integrability
item.description: For over two decades, the orbit-averaged precession equations of spinning binary black holes at second post-Newtonian order have been a standard model for their spin dynamics. One of their constants of motion, the projected effective spin, underlies the stability analysis of aligned-spin configurations and the construction of analytical solutions. The system is known to be Hamiltonian and integrable, its Hamiltonian being the orbit average of the full post-Newtonian Hamiltonian. Independently, we derive this… — Tom Colin, Sashwat Tanay, Manuel Alva-Morales, Prateek Anand — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO

item.title: On regularity-free characterization of bisymmetric means
item.description: We prove that every reflexive, bisymmetric binary operation on a non-degenerate real interval that is strictly increasing in each variable is automatically continuous and is a weighted quasi-arithmetic mean. This settles the reflexive, strictly increasing case of the automatic-continuity problem without assuming symmetry. The proof constructs a symmetric mean as the unique fixed point of a natural increasing operation and then applies the known symmetric automatic-continuity theorem. Maksa's method, combined with… — Gergely Kiss, Kazuki Okamura — arXiv math.AP / CA / FA / CV / SP / OA

item.title: Nonradial threshold scattering for the planar cubic--quintic NLS
item.description: We study the planar cubic--quintic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation \[ i\partial_tu+\Delta u=-|u|^2u+|u|^4u, \qquad (t,x)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2, \] with initial data $u_0\in H^1_x(\mathbb R^2)$. We prove scattering in both time directions when the mass of \(u_0\) equals the mass of the ground state for the focusing cubic equation. This resolves the nonradial threshold scattering problem posed by Murphy [\emph{Comm.\ Partial Differential Equations} \textbf{46} (2021), 2213--2234]. Together with the known… — Bo Yang, Lei Zhang, Bin Liu — arXiv math.AP / CA / FA / CV / SP / OA

item.title: Torsion order and the next-to-top term of knot Floer homology
item.description: Sivek conjectured that, for every nontrivial knot $K\subset S^3$, the dimension of the next-to-top term of $\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(K)$ is at least that of the top term. We show that this inequality holds for knots with $U$-torsion order one in either the minus theory $\mathrm{HFK}^-$ or the unoriented theory $\mathrm{HFK}'$. Combined with Eftekhary's work, this implies that knots with rational unknotting number one satisfy the conjecture. In particular, the result applies to every nontrivial satellite knot whose… — Kai Zhu — arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / KT / CT / arXiv: floer

item.title: Landau's problems through ratios of $L$-functions
item.description: Very recently, Lee announced a proof of the Twin Prime Conjecture assuming the Ratios Conjecture for the Riemann zeta function. We obtain conditional asymptotic formulas with power-saving errors for each of Landau's four prime problems. In the function field setting, using Sawin's estimates for factorization functions in squarefree progressions and a discriminant cohomology argument, we obtain unconditional Goldbach and prime-pair asymptotics over sufficiently large fixed odd fields, including prime fields… — Haozhe Gou, Victor Y. Wang, Max Wenqiang Xu — arXiv: primes / arXiv: riemann

item.title: Why should $\mathbbZ$ be Diophantine in $\mathbbQ$?
item.description: We give a Diophantine definition of the integers in the rational numbers conditional on the $abc$ conjecture, Dickson's conjecture, and finiteness of $2$-primary parts of Shafarevich--Tate groups. We also discuss some consequences of the existence of a Diophantine definition of the integers in the rational numbers. The goal of this work is to serve as an entry point to recent developments around Hilbert's tenth problem for the rational numbers. — Alexander Kozachinskiy, Hector Pasten, Xavier Vidaux — arXiv: elliptic

item.title: An alternate proof of the QMA lower bound for set-size estimation
item.description: In the set-size estimation query task, a query algorithm decides whether an $N$-bit input has Hamming weight $\ge B$ or $\le A$ (with $\ge B$ as the yes instances and $\le A$ as the no instances). When $B = 2A$, this is sometimes called approximate counting. The query complexity for this problem with a quantum witness (i.e., $\mathsf{QMA}$ query bounds) was resolved by Aaronson, Kothari, Kretschmer, and Thaler (CCC 2020) and proved using Laurent polynomials. Here we give a morally similar but distinct proof of… — Chinmay Nirkhe — arXiv: additive

item.title: Forward Self-similar Solutions of the Incompressible Navier-Stokes Equations in Dimensions Five and Higher
item.description: We construct forward self-similar solutions to the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n\ge 5$) for arbitrary $(-1)$-homogeneous, divergence-free initial data $u_0$ smooth on the unit sphere. For $n\ge 6$, the $O(|y|^{-3})$ bound on the nonlinear residual of the linear heat profile no longer yields $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$-integrability, obstructing a direct global energy perturbation around $e^Δu_0$. To overcome this difficulty, we truncate $u_0$ near the origin via a divergence-free cutoff… — Baishun Lai, Ruiyi Zhang, Xiaoxin Zheng — arXiv: navier

item.title: A Diophantine definition of $\mathbbZ$ in $\mathbbQ$
item.description: We prove that the integers form a Diophantine subset of the rational numbers. More precisely, there exist an integer $n\ge1$ and a polynomial $P\in\mathbb{Z}[T,W_1,\dots,W_n]$ of total degree at most four such that $q\in\mathbb{Q}$ is an integer if and only if $P(q,\mathbf w)=0$ for some $\mathbf w\in\mathbb{Q}^n$. Consequently, any recursively enumerable subset of $\mathbb{Q}^r$ is Diophantine, and Mazur's conjecture on the topology of rational points fails. The proof is inspired by OpenAI's work on Hilbert's… — Ashay Burungale — arXiv: elliptic / arXiv: modularity

item.title: High-frequency gravitational-wave backreaction on Levi-Civita spacetime: Rao geometry, Einstein-Rosen extension, and flat limits
item.description: Author(s): László Árpád Gergely, Attila Fóris, and Kata Karácsonyi We derive the leading backreaction of high-frequency gravitational waves on the Levi-Civita spacetime parametrized by the Komar mass density ${μ}_{K}$, using the Isaacson formalism with Brill-Hartle averaging. The high-frequency gravitational-wave amplitude decays radially independently of ${μ}_{K}$… [Phys. Rev. D 114, 104061] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026 — László Árpád Gergely, Attila Fóris, Kata Karácsonyi — Phys. Rev. D 114, 104061 (2026) / Physical Review D

item.title: Scale-separated quasi-dS and the Swampland
item.description: Ideas from the Swampland program (dS conjecture and TCC) suggest that it is impossible to obtain solutions of string theory/M-theory in the weak-coupling regions describing our current universe, with $V>0$, $\|\nabla V\|/V < 2/\sqrt{d-2}$ and $V \ll m^2$ (scale-separated "quasi-dS") where $m$ is the mass of the light tower. We test this expectation in M-theory compactifications and find that even after including the quantum effect of Casimir energy, for hyperbolic and (rigid) Riemann-flat manifolds, de Sitter… — Rafael Álvarez-García, Ivano Basile, Shi Chen, Cumrun Vafa — arXiv: swampland

item.title: Extremal Projectors and the Virasoro Algebra
item.description: Extremal projectors are universal operators projecting onto the highest weight space in a representation. Their existence and uniqueness (as formal series) are known for a broad range of Lie superalgebras and quantum groups. We consider a class of Lie superalgebras that contains reductive finite-dimensional Lie algebras as well as the Virasoro algebra. We prove the existence and uniqueness of an extremal projector for this class. The existence proof is given in terms of a recursive algorithm which can be used to… — Jonas T. Hartwig, Sagar Shrivastava — arXiv math-ph / nlin.SI / arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / RA / AC

item.title: Proof of the Quasi Riemann Hypothesis using $\mathbb Q[i]$
item.description: Using quartic Gauss sums in place of the cubic Gauss sums in OpenAI's original proof, we prove that the Dedekind $ζ$-function $ζ_{\mathbb Q(i)}(s)$ of $\mathbb Q(i)$ has no zeros in the half-plane $\Re s>599/600$, thereby obtaining the same zero-free half-plane for the Riemann $ζ$-function.We obtain the upper bound for the smoothed sum by applying Poisson summation twice and using the functional equation of the quartic Kubota series of angular weight $1$.In the Mellin representation, a zero-density bound for the… — XinHang Ji — arXiv: riemann

item.title: Functorial height and Orlov's rationality conjecture
item.description: An exceptional collection in the derived category of a smooth projective variety may fail to generate the whole category, and this failure cannot be detected by K-theory or by Hochschild homology. Kuznetsov's height detects it through Hochschild cohomology, that is, through natural transformations from the identity functor to its shifts. We replace the identity functor by an arbitrary endofunctor $F$ and define the height of a collection with coefficient $F$. It controls, in a range of degrees, the restriction of… — Xun Lin, Shizhuo Zhang — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / RA / AC

item.title: Stafford's conjecture on cyclicity of torsion modules
item.description: We prove that over a Weyl algebra over a field of characteristic zero $A_n(k)$, every nonzero $d\in A_n(k)$ admits $F,R,S\in A_n(k)$ such that $1=dR+FdS$, a conjecture Stafford proposed in 1978. As a consequence, every finitely generated torsion right $A_n(k)$-module is cyclic. The proof maps $d$, by a symplectic change of variables, to a normal form $\tilde d$ and shows that the cyclic module $Q=A_n(k)/(\tilde dA_n(k)+x_1^N\tilde dA_n(k))$ vanishes. We first show that right multiplication by $x_1$ is surjective… — Christopher Albert, Johanna Moser, Maximilian Philipp — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / RA / AC

item.title: Surrogate Modeling and Reduced-Order Methods in Gravitational-Wave Physics and Numerical Relativity: From Spectral Representations to Adaptive Compression
item.description: The rapid expansion of gravitational-wave astronomy and high-precision numerical relativity has created an acute computational bottleneck: direct numerical integration of the Einstein field equations and high-dimensional Bayesian parameter estimation require millions of waveform evaluations that cannot be sustained by traditional solvers alone. Reduced-order modeling (ROM) and surrogate techniques have emerged as foundational tools to bridge this gap, compressing high-fidelity solution manifolds into compact… — Manuel Tiglio — arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG / cs.LO / cs.CL (AI for math) / arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / arXiv: grav waves

item.title: Weak Hilbert's Nullstellensatz for skew polynomials over division rings
item.description: We establish a weak Nullstellensatz for skew polynomial rings $R_n=D[x_1,\ldots,x_n;\sigma]$, where $D$ is a division ring and the commuting variables induce the same automorphism $\sigma$ of $D$. For $n\ge2$, we characterize the pairs $(D,\sigma)$ for which every maximal left ideal is generated by $x_1-a_1,\ldots,x_n-a_n$, with $\sigma(a_j)a_i=\sigma(a_i)a_j$. The criterion consists of right $\sigma$-algebraic closure of $D$ and right algebraic closure of the centralizers of all commuting $(n-2)$-tuples in each… — Dinh Van Hoang, Vo Ngoc Thieu, Phan Thanh Toan — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / RA / AC

item.title: Sharp orthonormal Strichartz estimates for the Schrodinger equation in all remaining cases
item.description: We study orthonormal Strichartz estimates for the free Schr\"odinger equation in homogeneous Sobolev spaces $\dot H^s$. We resolve the remaining open cases concerning the optimal summability of the coefficients. Together with earlier results and counterexamples, our theorems complete the classification for nonnegative Sobolev regularity $0\le s — Yinghao Gong, Sonae Hadama, Shunya Toyoshima — arXiv math.AP / CA / FA / CV / SP / OA

item.title: Comment on "Exact, nonsingular black holes from a phantom DBI field as primordial dark matter"
item.description: We demonstrate that the metric and scalar configuration proposed in Ref.~[1] do not satisfy the complete set of field equations of the Dirac-Born-Infeld (DBI) field theory minimally coupled to general relativity on a radial domain containing the event horizon. The physical DBI branch for this gravitational setup terminates outside the event horizon. Thus, the proposed configuration does not describe a black hole solution of that theory. — Mustapha Azreg-Ainou, Marco A. A. de Paula — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / arXiv hep-ph / hep-ex / hep-lat / arXiv hep-th

item.title: Cameron--Martin theorem for SLE welding measures
item.description: For $\kappa\in(0,4]$, we prove a Cameron--Martin theorem for the welding law induced by SLE$_\kappa$ loop measure. Under simultaneous left and right composition $h\mapsto\varphi\circ h\circ\psi^{-1}$, the transformed law is mutually absolutely continuous with respect to the original law exactly when both maps belong to the Weil--Petersson group, and is mutually singular otherwise. Thus the Weil--Petersson group is the quasi-invariance group of the welding law under composition on either side. We also prove that… — Shuo Fan — arXiv math.AP / CA / FA / CV / SP / OA / arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / RA / AC / arXiv math.PR / DS / ST / OC / NA

item.title: Faster polynomial-space algorithms for poset problems
item.description: We give a polynomial-space, deterministic, exact algorithm for counting linear extensions of partial orders over $n$ elements, with running time $O^*((2\sqrt{2})^{n}) \subseteq O(2.829^n)$. This improves upon the long-standing bound of $O^*(4^{n})$ attainable by standard divide and conquer (Savitch 1970, Gurevich and Shelah 1987). Our algorithm uses a similar balanced splitting approach as the classical algorithm, but applies it only to the elements outside a largest antichain. For the elements of the antichain… — Laszlo Kozma, Junqi Tan — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.DM / cs.CC / cs.DS

item.title: Global existence for the 1D compressible Euler equations with time-decaying damping and spatial perturbations
item.description: We study the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional compressible Euler equations with damping coefficient $b(t)+a(x)$, where $b(t)=\lambda(1+t)^{-\mu}$ with $0<\mu<1$, $\lambda>0$, or $\mu=1$, $\lambda>2$, and $a\in C_b^1(\mathbb R)\cap L^1(\mathbb R)$ is nonnegative. We prove global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions for sufficiently small $C_b^1$ perturbations of a constant state, without assuming spatial decay or convergence of the initial data at infinity. No smallness condition is imposed on the… — Yuusuke Sugiyama — arXiv math.AP / CA / FA / CV / SP / OA

item.title: Incidence methods for algebraic expanders over arbitrary fields
item.description: Let $A\subset F$ be finite, $N=|A|$, $p=\operatorname{char}F$ (with $p=\infty$ in characteristic zero), and $L=1+\log(2N)$. In the range $N\le p^{1/2}$, we establish \[ |AA+A|\gg N^{129/85}L^{-72/85}. \] This improves the long-standing $3/2$-exponent bound for $AA+A$ in positive characteristic in the range $N\le p^{1/2}$, without any assumption on the multiplicative doubling of $A$. We further establish uniform expansion bounds with exponents $129/85$ and $32/21$ for four families of three-variable… — Yao Zhi — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.DM / cs.CC / cs.DS / arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / RA / AC

item.title: Connectivity of Matroids with Breadth-Critical Tangles
item.description: We construct an explicit infinite sequence of nonnegative integers $(s_0,s_1,\ldots)$ such that, for every $k\ge2$, every finite matroid with a breadth-critical tangle of order at least $k$ is $(s_0,s_1,\ldots,s_{k-2})$-connected. The constants $s_i$ depend only on $i$. This proves a conjecture of Brettell, Jowett, Oxley, Semple, and Whittle. — Zhuo Li, Zhen Chen — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.DM / cs.CC / cs.DS

item.title: Deep learning spacetime from entanglement dynamics
item.description: In the eternal AdS black hole, the entanglement of the thermofield double state is geometrically realised by the Einstein--Rosen bridge, in line with the ER=EPR conjecture. Hartman--Maldacena surfaces threading this bridge pass behind the event horizon, so the time-dependent entanglement entropy $S(t)$ of a pair of half-lines, one on each boundary, probes the black hole interior. We turn this relation around and ask how much of the bulk spacetime can be reconstructed from $S(t)$, using a neural ordinary… — Hyun-Sik Jeong, Keun-Young Kim, Gaya Yun, Kwan Yun — arXiv hep-th

item.title: Circuit spectra for binary matroids
item.description: The circuit spectrum of a matroid is defined to be the set of circuit sizes. The circuit $e$-spectrum of a matroid is the set of circuit sizes of the matroid containing the element $e$. The circuit spectrum problem is an important problem. Erd\H{o}s (1992) conjectured that every connected graph $G$ with girth $g$ and average degree $d$ has a cycle spectrum of size at least $\Omega(d^{\lfloor (g-1)/2 \rfloor})$. Sudakov and Verstra\"{e}te (2008) proved the full conjecture of Erd\H{o}s in a stronger form. It is… — Bing Wei, Haidong Wu, Shunzhe Zhang — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.DM / cs.CC / cs.DS

item.title: Counterexamples to Ecker's Conjecture
item.description: Analogous to Perelman's W-entropy defined for Ricci flow, K. Ecker defined a functional W for the mean curvature flow in R^{n+1} and the region it encloses, and made the conjecture that this functional is monotonically increasing in time. In this paper, we give a negative answer to Ecker's conjecture. — Jiarui Chen, Jie Wang — arXiv: ricci

item.title: Optimal local gradient estimate for gravity water waves and its application to the Stokes conjecture
item.description: In 1880, G. Stokes [Mathematical and Physical Papers, Vol. I] studied a two-dimensional gravity water wave and conjectured that the wave crest forms a symmetric corner of angle 2pi/3 at the stagnation point. The conjecture was first proved by Amick, Fraenkel, and Toland [Acta Math. 148 (1982)] and, independently, by Plotnikov [Dinamika Sploshn. Sredy 57 (1982)] via the Nekrasov integral equation. item.description: Author(s): Mark Ho-Yeuk Cheung It has been proposed that applying a rational filter to a black hole ringdown gravitational waveform reveals a direct wave component sourced near the event horizon. item.title: Optimal universal sets for submodular functions
item.description: We resolve the question of deterministic non-adaptive algorithms for nonnegative submodular maximization: We prove that for every $n \geq 2$ and $\epsilon \in (0,\frac{1}{4})$, there is a polynomial-size family ${F}_{n,\epsilon}$, $|{F}_{n,\epsilon}| = n^{O(1/\epsilon^2 \log (1/\epsilon))}$, such that for every nonnegative submodular function $f:2^{[n]} \to {\bf R}$, $\max_{S \in {F}_{n,\epsilon}} f(S) \geq (1/4 - \epsilon) \max_{S \subseteq [n]} f(S)$. item.title: The shape function of last passage percolation up to constants
item.description: We determine the diagonal shape function of lattice last passage percolation up to dimension-dependent constants and characterize its finiteness by a tail integral. The proof transfers estimates from an entropy-controlled Poisson model whose quadratic penalty makes the curvature dependence explicit. For critical tails of exponent $q$ in dimension $q\geq 2$, the mean passage time has order $n(\log n)^{(q+1)/(2q)}$, proving sharpness of the logarithmic exponent in the lower bound of Ganguly, Ginsburg and Nam. — Jnaneshwar Baslingker, Daniel Spivak, Balint Virag — arXiv math.PR / DS / ST / OC / NA

item.title: Isabelle Pool Server: a pooled verification service for prover training and multi-agent proving
item.description: Isabelle Pool Server (IPS), a verification service with a pool of warm headless Isabelle sessions behind an HTTP API, with session leasing and reclamation, memory-aware admission control, and a time budget on every call. Its verification interface spans single-step execution, block-level proof checking and whole-theory builds, with checkpoints for cheap branching and backtracking, and a build from scratch as the final arbiter. item.title: Time-Decay Rates toward a Rarefaction-Contact-Shock Composite Wave for the One-Dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations
item.description: We consider the one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier equations when the end states are connected by a rarefaction wave, a contact discontinuity, and a shock. item.title: Separability of coupled gravitational perturbations in Plebański--Demiański spacetimes
item.description: Recently, a major breakthrough in the separability of gravitational perturbations of the Kerr--Newman rotating charged black hole was achieved by Hintz [arxiv:2609.33661], and extended to non-zero cosmological constant Kerr--Newman-(A)dS black holes by Yoshida [arxiv:2610.20500] and Zhao [arxiv:2610.22274]. item.title: Symplectic $\mathbbCP^n$ recognition and filling rigidity via Rabinowitz Floer homology
item.description: We prove that a symplectic manifold $X$ admitting a pseudo-holomorphic line through two generic points, formulated as the non-vanishing of a genus zero Gromov--Witten invariant, is (rationally) homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb{CP}^n$, with identical first Chern class and quantum cohomology. item.title: Semi-Implicit and Convex Splitting Schemes for the Surface Cahn--Hilliard Equation on Curved Closed Surfaces
item.description: The surface Cahn--Hilliard equation describes phase separation and coarsening of a conserved composition field on fixed curved surfaces. We study a mixed $hp$-surface finite element discretization with curvilinear high-order elements, primarily on the sphere, with the stabilized semi-implicit BDF2 integrator and a stabilized convex-splitting variant solved with the same factorization. item.title: Quantum Born Geometries from Modular Quantization
item.description: A structural link between quantization and "thermal-doubled" non-commutative Born geometry (with its split-quaternionic structure) is uncovered via Tomita-Takesaki first-quantized modular theory for complexified and polarized ortho-symplectic spaces. item.title: Invariant solitons of the inverse mean curvature flow in the sphere and in hyperbolic space
item.description: We study hypersurfaces of the sphere $\mathbb{S}^n$ and of hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$, $n\ge 3$, that move under the inverse mean curvature flow by a one-parameter group of isometries. No closed hypersurface has this property, and a soliton with constant mean curvature is an open subset of a horosphere. item.title: Local-global compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed (co)homology of $\mathrmGL_2$ over CM fields
item.description: For each place $v \mid p$ such that $F_v \simeq \mathbf{Q}_p$, we establish a compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed homology with integral coefficients for $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over CM fields $F$ with $[F:\mathbf{Q}]>2$, after localization with respect to a non-Eisenstein decomposed generic maximal ideal of a Hecke algebra. — Jelena Ivancic — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / RA / AC / arXiv: langlands

item.title: Finite element nonlinear nudging for the Navier-Stokes equations
item.description: Nonlinear nudging augments the classical linear nudging (continuous data as- similation) term with a nonlinear feedback that strengthens as the observed error decreases, and yields super-exponential convergence to the true state. In this paper, we study nonlinear nudging for the 3-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with the finite element method, which allows complex geometries and physical boundary conditions. item.title: On the self-extensions of the mod $p$ Jacquet-Langlands correspondence over $\mathbbQ_p$
item.description: Let $p\ge5$ and $D$ be the unique nonsplit quaternion algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We compute, in the category of smooth representations with a fixed central character, the self-extension groups of the $D^{\times}$-representations occurring in the mod $p$ Jacquet-Langlands correspondence in the generic case. item.title: automodel: A Skill for Agentic Model Discovery
item.description: The search for better models, whether expressed as analytical equations or neural architectures, has increasingly shifted from manual design toward data-driven automation. While a multitude of algorithms exist, ranging from exhaustive search to AlphaEvolve, recent advances in general-purpose coding agents such as Claude Code and OpenAI Codex raise the question: could providing such systems with a "model discovery recipe" be enough to discover or improve models? item.title: Spectral action in Betti metaplectic Langlands
item.description: We construct the spectral action in the context of Betti metaplectic Langlands theory. More precisely, we prove that the category of twisted sheaves on $\text{Bun}_G$ with nilpotent singular support admits a canonical action by the symmetric monoidal category of quasicoherent sheaves on the moduli of twisted $H$-local systems, where $H$ is the metaplectic dual group. item.title: Structure Constants of Planar N=4 SYM at Any Coupling
item.description: We recast a recent conjecture for structure constants in planar N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory in a separation-of-variables-inspired form suitable for non-perturbative analysis. All state-dependent information enters through the quantum spectral curve. As a showcase, we compute at finite coupling the three-point functions of two half-BPS operators and the spin-two member of the Konishi multiplet. item.title: A geometric Kähler--Ricci flow proof of the Calabi--Yau theorem
item.description: We give a geometric proof that every Kähler class on a compact Kähler manifold with vanishing real first Chern class contains a unique Ricci-flat metric, and that the Kähler--Ricci flow converges smoothly to this metric. item.title: Invariant distributions and common denominators in the Bernstein center
item.description: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over a non-Archimedean local field. We conjecture that every invariant distribution whose support is compact modulo conjugation belongs to the rational Bernstein center. item.title: Heat-wave semigroup estimates and the compressible Navier-Stokes Equations
item.description: We study the connection between the heat-wave semigroup and the compressible Navier-Stokes (CNS) equations. item.title: Mean curvature flow into an ambient Riemannian manifold evolving by Ricci-Bourguignon flow
item.description: We study the mean curvature flow in Riemannian manifolds evolving by the Ricci-Bourguignon flow. Using DeTurck's trick, we establish short-time existence and uniqueness for the mean curvature flow in this time-dependent ambient geometry. item.title: Parisi Energy before Parisi Geometry in the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
item.description: The fractured low-energy landscape of spin glasses presents a notorious barrier to optimization. While high-depth calculations indicate that the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) can approach the Parisi ground-state energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass, how it does so remains elusive. item.title: Pair Correlation Conjecture for the Zeros of Artin $L$-functions I: Simple and Critical Zeros
item.description: In 1973, Montgomery posed the pair correlation conjecture (PCC) for the zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Motivated by PCC, Montgomery conjectured that the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function are almost surely simple, and proved that at least $2/3$ are simple assuming the Riemann hypothesis (RH). item.title: Vanishing Dissipation Limit to Planar Euler Shock for the Full Compressible Navier-Stokes Equations in $\mathbbR^3$
item.description: We prove the vanishing dissipation limit to a weak planar Euler shock for the full compressible Navier--Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$. The viscosity and heat conductivity are proportional to $\varepsilon$, with their ratio fixed. The conservative initial perturbation may depend on all three spatial variables and is assumed small only in the scaled $H^2 \cap \dot H^{-1}$ norm. No $L^1$ bound or zero-mass condition is required. item.title: Solution Spaces of the Minimal Surface and Monge-Ampère Equations near Infinity
item.description: In this paper, we study the constructions of all solutions to the minimal surface equation and the Monge-Ampère equation near infinity and the parametrization of these solutions by harmonic functions. It is well-known that Dirichlet boundary value problems in exterior domains do not always admit solutions. We demonstrate that prescribing asymptotic behaviors forms a new type of problem leading to all solutions near infinity. item.title: $\mathbb Z$ is diophantine over $\mathbb Q$ with 26 unknowns
item.description: Recently, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. Motivated by this work, G. item.title: Prime values of linear forms and a quadratic form: one proof and two arithmetic applications
item.description: Let $L_1,\dots,L_k\in \mathbb Z[x,y]$ be a system of linear polynomials whose homogeneous parts are pairwise linearly independent. Let $K=\mathbb Q(α)$ be an imaginary quadratic field. item.title: The additive ambiguity of gravitational entropy fixed by the topology of the horizon
item.description: In quantum gravity the algebra of observables of a subregion is of type III$_1$ at leading order in the semiclassical expansion, and it becomes of type II once the gravitational constraint is imposed. Hence generalized entropy acquires a trace, however it is defined only up to an additive constant. item.title: Pluriclosed flow on Kähler manifolds
item.description: We prove the maximal existence conjecture for pluriclosed flow on Kähler backgrounds. This leads to a priori generalizations of the Aubin-Yau and Calabi-Yau theorems, and resolves the question of connectedness of generalized Kähler structures on Calabi-Yau backgrounds. — Jeffrey Streets — arXiv: hodge

item.title: Uniqueness of tangent flows in mean curvature flow (I): smooth minimal cone
item.description: We prove uniqueness of multiplicity-one minimal-cone tangent flows in mean curvature flow when the cone has a smooth embedded two-sided link and satisfies strict Hardy stability, radial Gaussian nonresonance, and weighted stationary rigidity. We also establish a discrete Lojasiewicz inequality, polynomial convergence rates, and rigidity among smooth self-shrinkers. In particular, these conclusions hold for all Simons cones $\mathcal C_{p,q}$ with $p,q \geq 1, p+q\geq 6$. — Hanbing Fang, Yongheng Han — arXiv: ricci

item.title: Asymptotically safe gravitational form factors from the proper-time flow equation
item.description: Author(s): Emiliano Maria Glaviano We study the renormalization group flow of nonlocal form factors in four-dimensional quantum gravity within the proper-time formalism at quadratic order in the curvature expansion. item.title: Non-Invertible Quantum Cellular Automata I: Microscopic Definition of Non-Invertible Symmetries
item.description: We introduce non-invertible quantum cellular automata (QCAs), defined as locality-preserving quantum channels that are dualizable and pure. This provides an operator-algebraic definition of non-invertible symmetries of quantum lattice systems, formulated in terms of their action on local operators. item.title: Astrophysical Constraints for Bosonic Dark Matter in and Around Quark Stars
item.description: We investigate the structure, stability, and mass-radius relations of compact stars composed of quark matter within the non-ideal MIT Bag Model mixed with self-interacting bosonic dark matter with a $φ^n$ self-interaction potential. item.title: Refined random matrix conjectures for zeros of $p$-adic $L$-functions
item.description: We make and test the conjecture that for $p$-adic $L$-functions associated to quadratic Dirichlet characters and their Teichmüller twists, all local statistics of zeros in the unit disk match those of $p$-adic random matrix eigenvalues. item.title: Turing Agent: Agentic Formal Verification for Mathematical Research
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly advancing mathematical discovery, moving beyond benchmark-level problem solving to tackle frontier research problems. item.title: Elliptic Gromov-Witten Invariants of Instanton Moduli
item.description: We calculate the genus $1$ Gromov-Witten invariants with one tautological divisor insertion of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}(r,n)$ of rank-$r$, $c_2=n$ torsion-free sheaves on $\mathbb{P}^2$ framed along the infinity divisor.
